scope: All 108 names: the text was compared name by name with the page images of the TTD book (pp. 24–28), and every meaning was read against its name. There are no word-by-word glosses on this page (the meanings are per name). The range-number flags are the block labels. The text agrees with the print throughout. Many names allude to the Veṅkaṭācala legends; the meanings of 46, 50 and 67 remain my best reading.

items.issue: Name 9, kumārākalpasevyāya, was “served by Kumāra and by Brahmā's kalpa”; ākalpa is “for a whole kalpa”.
items.change: Now “worshipped by Kumāra (Skanda) for a whole kalpa”.

items.issue: Name 18, śaṅkharājanya-, was “the king of conch-bearers”; it is King Śaṅkha, who saw the Lord on the hill.
items.change: Now “seen by the lotus eyes of King Śaṅkha”.

items.issue: Name 46, vākpatibrahmadātre, was “giver of the lord of speech and of Brahmā”.
items.change: Now “who gave Bṛhaspati, lord of speech, the knowledge of Brahman”.

items.issue: Name 74 was “on whose account Lakṣmī did penance”; the compound makes him the ascetic, for Lakṣmī's sake, at the golden-lotus pool.
items.change: Now “who did penance for Lakṣmī on the bank of the golden-lotus pool”.

items.issue: Names 83, 85: “giver of Añjanā's son” and “fond of priyaṅgu fruit” (priyaṅgu is a millet).
items.change: Now “who gave Añjanā a son” and “whose favourite food is priyaṅgu millet”.

items.issue: Name 92, -vedāntadeśikatvapradāya, was “who gave the brahmin Kṛṣṇa the teaching of the Vedānta”; deśikatva is the office of teacher.
items.change: Now “who made the brahmin named Kṛṣṇa a teacher of Vedānta”.

items.issue: Name 106 was “giver of the full fruit of the world's holy places, as Balarāma”; Balarāma (Halāyudha) is the one who receives it.
items.change: Now “who gave Balarāma the whole fruit of the world's holy places”.

items.issue: Name 50: “bend in blessing” blurred vara and ānamra.
items.change: Now “whose shining hands hold the conch and discus and are lowered to grant boons”.

items.issue: In the print every name is followed by the refrain “śrī veṅkaṭeśāya namaḥ”; the page did not say so.
